behavior: The manual Default implementation explicitly evaluates B::default before T::default, independently of BoundingNode field declaration order chosen for object-before-bounds destruction.

A bounds-construction failure prevents object construction. An object-construction failure destroys the completed bounds and no uninitialized object. Exact native phase traces are checked from the committed native expected file.
Completed nodes are detached roots and leaves. On destruction the object precedes bounds, and both destructor callbacks retain their original boxed field addresses.

Throwing native member destructors explicitly use noexcept(false). Matching Rust panic tests prove completed-member destruction order and original addresses for either failing member, with strict Miri checking Rust Box cleanup.

The new implementation requires only Default on each payload; it does not require Clone or BoundingVolume. Existing constructors, collection generic bounds, public fields, lifetime variance, auto-traits and borrowed payload acceptance remain unchanged.

Rust borrowed and zero-sized payload defaults are tested as Rust-safe supported domains. Scalar Rust Default produces initialized zero values; the native private constructor default-initializes scalar members without initialization, so scalar value equivalence is not claimed.
Existing payload and new default native probes share one extracted trace header; prior native rows are unchanged. Historical receipt hashes and archived source snapshots remain intact.
